biography: Loris Cabirou, a Monaco native, didn't come from motorsport royalty. His father ran a small bistro overlooking the harbor, and Loris spent his childhood watching the yachts, not the race cars. That changed during the Monaco Grand Prix when he was ten. A rogue tire, flung over the barrier, landed near his feet, igniting a fire within him. He began karting with a second-hand machine, fueled by a borrowed passion. His raw talent quickly became evident, dominating local circuits. After a brief stint in Formula Renault, funding dried up. Undeterred, Cabirou transitioned to GT racing, where his flashy style and unwavering confidence caught the eye of Lamborghini. Now, at the peak of his career, he aims for the GT World Challenge title, proving that passion and talent can overcome any obstacle.
drivingStyle: Cabirou's driving style is a blend of calculated aggression and flamboyant showmanship. He's known for late-braking maneuvers that often leave rivals scrambling. He possesses an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from his Lamborghini, even when the car is on the edge. Tire management isn't his strongest suit, often pushing them to their absolute limit in pursuit of a faster lap. Under pressure, Cabirou thrives, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest, feeding off the energy of the crowd.

rivalries.reason: Rossi, a meticulous and technical driver, clashes with Cabirou's impulsive style. Their on-track battles are legendary, often ending in controversial overtakes and heated exchanges in the paddock.
Moreau, a rising star in GT racing, views Cabirou as an old guard blocking her path to the top. Their rivalry is fueled by ambition and a desire to prove who is the fastest GT driver.

Tanaka, known for his zen-like calm, finds Cabirou's flashy antics disrespectful to the sport. Their contrasting personalities often lead to tense moments during press conferences and driver briefings.

quirks: Always wears a lucky blue bracelet given to him by his grandmother.
Listens to classical music before every race to calm his nerves.
Refuses to start a race without polishing his helmet visor to a mirror shine.
famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Spa in 2020, battling through treacherous conditions and a late-race safety car period to secure a hard-fought victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2018 GT World Challenge final race, costing him the championship.
